questions.question: When a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Do what the other cars are doing, even if the guard says something different.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if there were no children present.

questions.explanation: Always obey a crossing guard's directions in a school zone. Be ready to slow down when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the streets.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for driving very carefully wherever children are present. Drive slowly near schools, playgrounds, and residential neighborhoods.

questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:
questions.explanation: A slippery road requires more distance to stop than a dry road does. Always keep a longer distance between your car and the car ahead when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: Before backing up, you should check behind your car for bikes, tricycles, and small children.
questions.explanation: Always look behind your car before you get in to back up. Check for bikes, tricycles, and small children. This is especially important if you drive a large vehicle like a van or truck.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down on a highway, turn on your hazard flashers and carefully exit the road. Park as far off the road as possible so other drivers can see you clearly. Open your hood to signal that your vehicle is disabled.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you do?

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are visible.
Signal only if other cars are nearby.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only during heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from the curb. Do not skip this step—it is the law, and it keeps everyone safe.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: Driving slower than the traffic around them.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When taking medicine, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Ask your doctor about how it will affect your driving.
Keep your window open and drive slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about how it will affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive safely. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how a medicine might impact your driving. This is especially important if you receive a prescription for a tranquilizer or sedative.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and rest, or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest, or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, take a break every hour or so on long trips. If possible, take turns driving with another person so you can sleep while they drive.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a road with a solid yellow line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken yellow line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken yellow line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to change lanes or pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. Always change lanes only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger?
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, move away from them. Avoid eye contact and don't use gestures that could upset them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers a steep hill is coming. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake problems.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves left, then right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves right and then left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if cars are coming toward you.
Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
Proceed carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only for traffic on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a full stop. Let vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection pass first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning signals, drivers should slow down, look, and listen.
questions.explanation: If there are no warning lights or gates, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains. Cross only when it is safe.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you won't have enough time to stop if the car ahead stops suddenly. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no crosswalk, drivers must stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, stop at the stop line if there is one. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, visibility is low. You can only see as far as your headlights. This makes it hard to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are going.
